**The computation (reproduced 11-04 from the formulas; the six cells match Table 3 to the second decimal).** Let $\tau(d)$ be the withholding rate on income at age $d$ days: 0.225 for $d\le180$, 0.20 for $180<d\le360$, 0.175 for $360<d\le720$, 0.15 beyond (Lei 11.033/2004). Let $\iota(d)$ be the IOF share of income: 0.96 on day 1 falling to 0 on day 30 (Decreto 6.306/2007); it does not bind in any cell below, since every age is at least 90 days. Let $r$ be the application's gross annual rate, set at the CDI, $a$ the age in days at the move, $h$ the horizon in days the money then stays invested.

- Stay: $W_s=1+[1-\tau(a+h)]\,[(1+r)^{(a+h)/365}-1]$.
- Move to a bank paying $r'$: $P=1+[1-\tau(a)][1-\iota(a)]\,[(1+r)^{a/365}-1]$, then $W_m(r')=P\,\{1+[1-\tau(h)]\,[(1+r')^{h/365}-1]\}$.
- Cost per R\$100: $100\,[W_s-W_m(r)]$. Break-even premium: $\pi=r^{*}-r$ with $W_m(r^{*})=W_s$, solved by bisection, in pp a year. Premium as a share of CDI: $100\,\pi/r$.

```
cells[6]{age_days,horizon_days,cost_per_100,premium_pp,premium_pct_cdi}:
  90,365,0.16,0.19,1.9
  200,180,0.43,1.13,11.3
  200,730,0.46,0.24,2.4
  400,365,0.71,0.79,7.9
  800,180,0.58,1.32,13.2
  800,730,0.62,0.28,2.8
```
